0.0.n: This noun names the machine used to buy train tickets.

0.1.n: Links the ticket machine to 上 to specify what the map is above.

0.2.n: Used with の to describe a position relative to the ticket machine.

0.3.n: Links the location 券売機の上 to the noun 路線図 that follows.

0.4.n: Refers to the diagram showing train lines and stations.

0.5.n: Marks the map as where you look for the station.

0.6.n: 行く changes to 行きたい to express desire and directly describes the following station.

0.7.n: The preceding 行きたい tells you which station: the one you want to visit.

0.8.n: Marks the station as the thing you are asked to look at.

0.9.n: The て-form of 見る plus ください makes a polite request.

1.0.n: Points back to the station you just found and must come before a noun.

1.1.n: Refers to the destination mentioned in the previous instruction.

1.2.n: Links the station to 下 to specify what the number is beneath.

1.3.n: Describes the number’s position relative to the station on the map.

1.4.n: Links the location その駅の下 to the following noun 数字.

1.5.n: Refers to the fare displayed beneath the station on the map.

1.6.n: Marks the number as the thing you are asked to look at.

1.7.n: The て-form of 見る plus ください makes a polite request.

2.0.n: Points to the number just identified and directly modifies 数字.

2.1.n: Refers to the figure printed beneath your destination station.

2.2.n: Identifies this number as what corresponds to the fare.

2.3.n: Usually means price; here it refers to the cost of the train journey.

2.4.n: Marks the resulting role in 値段になる: the number serves as the fare.

2.5.n: なる usually expresses becoming; here it explains what the displayed number represents.

2.6.n: Connects the fare explanation to the resulting instruction by giving a reason.

2.8.n: Again points to the displayed number and comes directly before 数字.

2.9.n: Provides the value you should match when selecting a fare.

2.10.n: Marks what is being compared with 同じ.

2.11.n: Used in Xと同じ to describe something matching X.

2.12.n: Refers to the fare option you select on the ticket machine.

2.13.n: Marks the fare as what you select.

2.14.n: The polite ます-form of 選ぶ describes the next step in the procedure.

3.0.n: お is a customary polite prefix attached to 金 in this everyday word.

3.1.n: Marks the money as what you insert.

3.2.n: 投入 combines with する; します is its polite form, used here to describe a procedural step.

4.0.n: This noun is being defined; it combines with する to form a verb.

4.1.n: Marks 投入 as the term whose meaning will be explained.

4.3.n: The plain dictionary form is quoted to explain the more formal word 投入.

4.5.n: Links the quoted verb 入れる to 意味.

4.6.n: Used to explain the definition of 投入.

0.lit: On the route map above the ticket machine, please look at the station you want to go to.
0.tip: 行きたい comes before 駅 to describe it: the station you want to go to.

1.lit: Please look at the number underneath that station.
1.tip: その駅の下の数字 chains two の links to identify the number underneath that station.

2.lit: Since this number serves as the fare, select the same fare as this number.
2.tip: Xと同じ means the same as X; と marks what you match.

3.tip: The polite ます-form can describe a procedural step rather than directly command the listener.

4.lit: As for insertion, it is the meaning of put in.
4.tip: 投入 is a formal noun; adding する makes the verb 投入する, explained here with the everyday verb 入れる.
